fixes.explanation: That number belongs to the first try at Ai. About three thousand men went up then, and they fled from the men of Ai (Joshua 7:4). This time the LORD tells Joshua, Israel's leader, “Take the whole army with you…” Three thousand is the first trip, and the whole army is this one.

True, baker. Joshua tells the men in ambush, “…you are to rise from the ambush and seize the city, for the LORD your God will deliver it into your hand.” That's the plan for while Israel is running away. Later the LORD tells Joshua to hold out his battle lance toward Ai, and as soon as he does, the men in ambush rise quickly (Joshua 8:18, 19). The ambush crew spends a lot of time waiting, and then they move fast.

North, baker! The troops “…camped to the north of it, with the valley between them and the city.” The other group lay in ambush to the west, between Bethel and Ai (Joshua 8:12). One group is in front of the city, and the other is set up behind it. The king of Ai did not know about the ambush (Joshua 8:14).

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The comparison implies that the first force was defeated because it was small, and that the same size force would produce the same result. The text does not give that reason.
The worn-out stamp comparison does not match the action in the passage. A worn stamp concerns the quality of a stamp, not the size of a force.
Saying one crew waves hello adds an action the text does not give.
